sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: Aesculus hippocastanum is a large deciduous tree that can exceed 25 m. Its opposite leaves are palmately divided into five to seven toothed leaflets. Upright clusters of cream-white flowers have yellow markings that turn red after pollination; the green, spiny capsule usually contains one glossy brown seed. The species is native from the central Balkans to Türkiye and is widely planted in parks.

sections.title: Toxicity and lookalikes
sections.text: Horse-chestnut seeds (conkers) are not edible and can cause illness if swallowed. They are distinct from the edible sweet chestnut, Castanea sativa; the fruits have different husks and the trees belong to different families.
